correctness.rationale: Rebuilt the zero-sum powered-distance expansion on bridge endpoints and uniform ordinary-vertex sums: the within-clique fluctuations yield −∑e_i²−∑f_j², optimizing the bridge mass S completes square −2(S+(2^p−2)(X−Y)/2)², leaving −(X,Y)M_qr(p)(X,Y)^T with the displayed real symmetric 2×2 Schur matrix. All parameters (X,Y,S) can be independently realized by a zero-sum vector, so p-negative type iff M_qr PSD. Its least eigenvalue is γ−β−sqrt(δ²+z²). On (1,2), z<0 because 2·3^p−4^p−2>0, and β′−z′=3^p ln3−2·2^p ln2>0. Thus β+sqrt(δ²+z²) increases strictly and crosses γ once between p=1 and p=2 (at 2 iff q=r=1). For p>2, β>2 makes both diagonal entries negative. Li–Weston propagation gives strict negative type below 1. Kernel dimensions then give Euclidean rank q+r at a nonexceptional threshold and 1 for the four-vertex path; below it the rank is q+r+1. Size monotonicity follows by decrementing the relevant diagonal entry and using a kernel vector with nonzero coordinates, asymptotic via implicit differentiation at p∞=ln2/ln(3/2). Independent all-vertex shortest path matrices yielded endpoint centered Gram ranks for (q,r)=(1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(3,4), confirming the exception and sample roots.
